newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr firms at close after featureless session.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr firms at close after featureless session.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended a featureless session on Wednesday much where it began but with a slightly bid tone.
It closed at US$0.7091/98 against its 0.7085/92 opening as shorts and exporters covered at the close.
On its Trade-Weighted Index, it ended at 66.88, up from the 66.76 opening.

Dealers said the only spark of interest was a rumour (given no credence) that a coalition agreement would be made tonight. However, talks between the parties, already in their sixth week, were routine today and all appears quiet at parliament.
The Labour and the Alliance parties are meeting this evening to thrash out the basis on which the Alliance would support a New Zealand First-Labour government, should NZ First side with Labour.

One dealer said the Kiwi was likely to suffer a 100 basis point sell-off if NZ First, which holds the balance of power, goes with left-of-centre Labour, and there would be a similar sized rally if it went with the ruling conservative National Party.
